feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital platforms, communications systems, and public-sector leadership. It is credible and well targeted, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with some formatting/style inconsistencies that reduce scanability and impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear professional brand: the headline and summary immediately communicate seniority, specialization, and sector fit.  
- Strong credibility: long progression at NACo plus concrete scope indicators like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers.”  
- Good breadth of expertise across strategy, platforms, analytics, governance, and multimedia, reinforced by relevant tools and recent projects.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition: “digital strategy,” “governance,” “workflows,” “platforms,” and “communications” recur heavily across sections; tighten to avoid overlap between Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT.  
- Improve structure/scanability: several roles use long paragraph-plus-dash formatting; convert to cleaner bullet formatting and prioritize outcomes/results over responsibility statements.  
- Fix style consistency issues: use one capitalization style for the name (“Coleman Davis” vs “Coleman DAVIS”); standardize punctuation around lists and compounds (“social, and multimedia” → “social and multimedia”); “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary and weakens the Education section. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear public-sector relevance, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and adding one or two concrete signals of scale would make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace the second sentence with a more outcome-oriented summary tied to recent work and leadership scope.
- Add a concrete scale marker already supported elsewhere, e.g. “10,000+ page platforms,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Reduce list-like phrasing; group capabilities into 2–3 themes rather than naming every function.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Led enterprise digital ecosystems supporting 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, and 50+ internal publishers, spanning Drupal modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial workflows, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and discovery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search and discovery” is more specific.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” is echoed throughout work experience, so keep the intro concise.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be sharper if phrased as concise capability areas rather than repeating full-value statements.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure; use shorter noun phrases.
- Prioritize the strongest, most distinctive areas first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation.
- Replace broader items like “advocacy and public-sector communications” with a more specific capability tied to delivery or systems.
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Multi-channel content operations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestreaming

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” and “AI-enabled…experiences” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- This section also overlaps substantially with Topline Skills; consider using one for strategic capabilities and the other for tools/platforms.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the wording and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it feel more additive and polished.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing to reinforce recency and distinguish this from work experience.
- Tighten parallel structure: start each item with a strong action verb and keep each description to one concise, outcome-oriented line.
- Standardize style: use “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently; spell out “10 x 20-foot” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider this rewrite: “Selected Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search—Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level chat. We Are Counties Microsite—Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources. Organization Anniversary Campaign—Created a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10 x 20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series—Launched a recurring advocacy video program spanning planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and the advocacy video series overlap with current/past role bullets; keep only if presented as selected highlights rather than restated duties.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.

- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Make it sharper by foregrounding scope, platform leadership, and any measurable outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter summary line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed and implemented digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Consolidate Drupal/CMS bullets: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, modular storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits; provided front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, publishing time reduced, search success uplift, or engagement gains from the AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this bullet shorter here.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also echo the header and NACo role—avoid repeating broad capability language.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It would be stronger if the opening were tighter, bullets started with clearer outcomes, and channel-management points were less repetitive with earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel bullet and add measurable results if available: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials; improved engagement/reporting through centralized channel strategy.”
- Make ops/analytics bullets more impact-driven: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to strengthen executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version at a higher strategic/organizational level.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed here as building enterprise capability (studio, scale, in-house production).

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and any concrete growth or process outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member-facing communications.”
- Combine and sharpen bullets around owned outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show build-out and impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable workflow/editorial outcomes if available: e.g., publishing volume, turnaround time, campaign cadence, stakeholder groups supported, or engagement growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved workflows” and “strengthened editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language; keep this version focused on hands-on execution.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; clarify this role as scaling/formalizing the series, not starting it.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS

- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating generic CMS terms without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery; **Integrations & deployment:** API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions; **Tagging & tracking:** Google Tag Manager
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use version-specific naming; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- Consider replacing broad terms with stronger phrasing if accurate: “REST API integrations,” “serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers),” “CI/CD automation (GitHub Actions).”
- If possible, connect to outcomes elsewhere in the CV by adding examples in experience bullets rather than here, e.g., tagging, deployment automation, or custom front-end work that improved launch speed or tracking quality.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may also overlap with GitHub Actions unless differentiated.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function to improve scanability: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Workflow Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses for stronger positioning, e.g. **Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana (cross-team planning)**
- Consider trimming lower-value/general tools if space is tight; keep the platforms most tied to recent systems/governance work

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; they add less differentiation than Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, or Asana

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems

Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, keep this as a concise platform list rather than repeating newsletter achievements.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In the Technical + IT section, keep it tighter and more tool-focused; move broader capabilities like SEO/A/B testing/dashboarding to a skills section unless you can make them more specific.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • KPI reporting**

- If A/B testing is important and current, specify platform/method: **A/B testing strategy** or name the tool; otherwise remove it
- Order by strongest/recent relevance: **GA4, Clarity, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio** first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This line substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one of the two
- “Dashboarding” is already implied by Looker Studio/Power BI, so it reads redundant

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer

Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.

- Reframe as early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”

Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations, improved publishing workflows, contributed to a major website refresh, and produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates. Provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this role as launching/producing the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating governance/operations language already used more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the distinctive innovation/research scope and tighten the media language.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the broader function, then the standout result: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities…”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with clearer ownership: “produced digital and multimedia content” or “supported development of digital and multimedia materials.”
- Tighten the podcast clause to show initiative and end-to-end execution: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”

- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item focused on innovation/research + first podcast.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here, since stronger, more recent evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
